newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti shares rise, but doubts weigh.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti shares rise, but doubts weigh.

text.p: Shares in Italy's Olivetti perked up on Monday after a key asset sale was clinched last week, but concerns remain over further sell-offs and the intentions of its former chairman and largest shareholder Carlo de Benedetti.

Information technology group Olivetti sold an indirect 5.8 percent stake in mobile phone consortium Omnitel to Mannesmann late Friday at what analysts described as a "fair price" in part of its 1.2 trillion lire ($1.8 billion) disposal plan.
The shares rose on the news and were up 6.05 percent at 480 lire at 1400 GMT, after hitting a high of 485 lire.

Olivetti bought the stake from Lehman Brothers for 283 billion lire in late 1995 pushing its total stake in Omnitel at the time to 41.3 percent, and also added 45 billion lire as part of an equity injection into Omnitel.

Olivetti's chief executive Roberto Colannino in September launched a disposal programme to raise 800 billion lire by the end of this year, and some 400 billion lire during 1997, and when completed will consider a capital increase in late 1997.

With the Omnitel stake sale raising just over half the amount, the sale of Tecnost and its ailing PC business set to be completed by the end of the year, are aimed at raising further cash. The flotation of part of office equipment company Lexikon is expected to be the main capital raising event of 1997.

"The Omnitel stake was always the easy bit to sell, Olivetti has got a good price but there are more difficult disposals to make and there is the shadow of a rights issue next year," said one industry analyst.

Analysts were left pondering de Benedetti's latest moves, after his French investment group Cerus sold its 20 percent stake last week in car parts group Valeo, and on Monday Spanish newspaper Expansion said de Benedetti through Cerus was looking for a single buyer for his 48.05 percent stake in Spain's Cofir.

Many analysts saw this as a tidying up of Benedetti's expansion moves of earlier years, cutting group debts, but some consider it might mark a move by de Benedetti to sell his stake in Olivetti. He holds a 15 percent stake through his group Cir.
Asked if it was possible Cir will pull out of Olivetti in an interview in French newspaper Le Monde last week, de Benedetti said, "In principle, Yes."

De Benedetti said in the interview he would put his money where he is working, and he no longer had a position at Olivetti. He added that he didn't think anyone would imagine that he could still invest in Olivetti.
He said the Valeo sale would help reduce Cir and Cerus debts, but the cash wouldn't go into Olivetti's coffers.

Milan's financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore commented in an article entitled "Rays of light and fog banks over group's future," that "The Engineer (de Benedetti) with these comments has in a way written his own first true conclusion for his 20 year adventure with Olivetti."

"This is a sweet and sour conclusion - sweet in the value which has emerged for Omnitel - sour in admitting that Cir - which now has the clear aim of reconverting the information technology group into a telecoms group - has bitten off more than it could chew," the paper added. ($1=1,515 lire)
